title: 3.7L engine cooling specifications
introduction:
I read this cooling reference by asking what each table answers: which coolant is listed, what mixture provides the stated freeze protection, which pressure applies, and when the thermostat opens. Keep the original-fluid and service-fluid tables distinct, and match the product form and specification as carefully as the name.

This is a specification guide for the Duratec application named above. Mixing compatibility, safe system access, filling, flushing and test methods require the matching service instructions; the tables alone do not establish those procedures.

edits.why: This table identifies the original orange coolant products and their listed fill capacity. Read the concentrated and prediluted entries as different supplied forms: concentrate is for mixing, while prediluted coolant arrives mixed. Match the product identifier and specification together.

The service table identifies yellow coolant in concentrated and prediluted forms, plus the cooling-system flush. Coolant rows carry a fill capacity; the dash beside the flush leaves its quantity unspecified.

Read each percentage pair in the heading’s order: antifreeze/coolant first, distilled water second. Then read across to its freeze-protection temperature. Keep the extreme-cold-climate qualifier attached to the row that carries it.

Match the row to the complete cooling system, pressure-relief cap or radiator test. The radiator-test value specifically applies with the radiator removed from the vehicle. Each pressure is given in kilopascals and pounds per square inch.

The thermostat controls coolant flow through the radiator circuit. Think of it as a gate that opens progressively: the starts-to-open range marks the beginning of movement, while the fully-open entry describes the later position. I keep those stages separate when reading the temperature specifications.
